paragraphs.text: Now he comes to another type of affections, which is in that part of the mind which men call covetous or desirous: and he reprehends fornication, covetousness, and jesting very sharply.
Jests which men cast at one another: that no lightness is seen, nor evil example given, nor any offence made by evil words or backbiting.

paragraphs.text: Because these sins are such that the most part of men do not consider them to be sins, he awakes the godly to the end that they should so much the more take heed to guard themselves from these sins as from most harmful plagues.
A bondslave to idolatry, for the covetous man thinks that his life consists in his goods.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Because we are most ready to follow evil examples, therefore the apostle warns the godly to always remember that the others are but as it were darkness, and that they themselves are as it were light. And therefore the others commit all evils (as men are accustomed to do in the dark), but they ought not to follow their examples, but rather (as the property of the light is) reprove their darkness, and to walk in such a way (having Christ that true light going before them) as it becomes wise men.

paragraphs.text: Now he descends to a family, dividing orderly all the parts of a family. And he says that the duty of wives consists in this, to be obedient to their husbands.
The first argument, for they cannot be disobedient to their husbands except by also resisting God, who is the author of this subjection.
A declaration of the former saying: because God has made the man head of the woman in marriage, as Christ is the head of the Church.

paragraphs.text: The husbands duty towards their wives is to love them as themselves, of which love the love of Christ towards his Church is a graphic image.

Because many men pretend the infirmities of their wives to excuse their own hardness and cruelty, the apostle wishes us to mark what manner of Church Christ received, when he joined it to himself, and how he does not reject her for all her filth, and uncleanness, but ceases not to wipe it away with his cleanness, until he wholly purifies it.
Make it holy.
